what: Packet timestamps of finished recordings (E2E build: synthetic display, real MediaRecorder, chunk upload and FFmpeg remux; every second recording paused once for 0.8 s). ffprobe packet pts/dts per stream; ffmpeg decode to the null muxer in the default constant-frame-rate mode and with -fps_mode vfr.

before.equalTimestampExample: first two video packets at 0 ms and 0 ms (then 32, 65, 99 ...)
before.decodeComplaintExample: Application provided invalid, non monotonically increasing dts to muxer in stream 0: 53 >= 53 (packet times 1699, 1751, 1783 ms: two frames fall into one 33 ms slot of the 30 fps grid; the packets themselves increase)

after.note: the remaining default-mode messages are ffmpeg re-timing a variable-frame-rate file onto a constant grid, not a property of the file; the tests assert strictly increasing packet timestamps and an error-free -fps_mode vfr decode instead

realFfmpeg: vendor/ffmpeg 9.0.2 for the remux; the test helpers use the same binaries (e2e) or the PATH ffmpeg 8.1.1 (native)
regressionTests: tests/unit/ffmpeg-integration.test.ts: input whose first two frames share a timestamp -> strictly increasing output, same packet count
tests/native/recording.native.spec.ts: assertCommon checks timestamps on every real recording
